_comment_plugins: Plugins are listed explicitly. Stryker's default discovery globs node_modules/@stryker-mutator/* , which pnpm's symlinked, content-addressed layout does not expose the same way npm's flat tree does - without this the runner fails with 'no TestRunner plugins were loaded' even though the package is installed.
_comment_scope: Scoped to pure, decision-dense domain logic where a wrong answer is a correctness or security failure. Line coverage answers 'was this executed'; mutation score answers 'would a test have noticed if it were wrong'. MEASURED COST: src/utils/redaction.ts alone (70 lines) produced 129 mutants and took 11 minutes at concurrency 4, running 78 tests per mutant - so scope is a budget decision, not a preference. Regex-dense files dominate the mutant count. src/experience/agent-bus.ts is deliberately EXCLUDED despite being high value: at 1137 lines it would dominate the nightly run, and its invariants are already covered by the fast-check property suite, which is a better tool for regex and decoder behaviour than operator mutation. Adapters (src/services, src/auth, src/azure), oclif command shells and the TUI are excluded because their behaviour is asserted by test/contract, test/chaos and test/integration, which this runner does not execute - every mutant there would survive for a reason that says nothing about test quality.
_comment_thresholds: break=60 is a floor, not a target. It fails the nightly job only on a real regression in the domain core; high=85 marks the aspiration. Measured baseline: src/utils/redaction.ts scored 83.72% (108 killed, 18 survived, 3 uncovered) - the survivors were almost entirely Regex-mutator variants, which is the genuine equivalent-mutant story for this codebase. Raise these as a ratchet once a full baseline run lands - never lower them to make a run pass.
